facts.text: An indicative physical-test matrix should be applied per machine family—wheeled rigid, articulated and tracked—and per brake or drive architecture.
facts.quote: An indicative matrix per machine family* (wheeled rigid, articulated, tracked) and per brake or drive architecture

facts.text: The indicative physical-test matrix includes a static latency sweep from command to pressure to 10% g, with at least 10 repetitions across oil temperatures.
facts.quote: a static latency sweep of command to pressure to 10% g, at least 10 repetitions across oil temperatures

facts.text: The indicative physical-test matrix includes straight-line stops at three speeds, two payloads, and both level ground and maximum design grade, with three repetitions for each combination.
facts.quote: straight-line stops at three speeds × two payloads × level and maximum design grade, three repetitions each

facts.text: The indicative physical-test matrix includes one low-speed surface-friction matrix covering hard, loose and wet surfaces.
facts.quote: one surface-friction matrix of hard, loose and wet surfaces at low speed

facts.text: For articulated machines, the indicative physical-test matrix includes stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope.
facts.quote: for articulated machines, stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope

facts.text: The indicative physical-test matrix totals roughly 60 to 100 instrumented runs per machine family.
facts.quote: That comes to roughly 60 to 100 instrumented runs per family

facts.text: Completing the indicative physical-test matrix within the validation window is achievable only if machine families share instrumentation.

facts.text: NIOSH's 2018 dynamic stopping tool analyzed brake force, grade, initial speed, lag and rolling resistance.
